ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the distribution of average sea-level pressure near Antarctica in January, marked with latitudes and longitudes such as 30°W, 60°W, 90°W and 30°S, 60°S. Great Wall Station is located near the Antarctic Peninsula, around about 60°S, and Ushuaia is located at the southern end of South America; between the two places is the Drake Passage. The isobars near the Great Wall Station–Ushuaia sailing section are relatively dense, and nearby there is a low-pressure center marked "Low", with pressure lines such as 984, 992, 1000, and 1004 visible around it. Reasoning: The ship sails from Great Wall Station toward Ushuaia, and its course is roughly from the Antarctic Peninsula side toward the southern end of South America, with northward and westward components. According to the rule for judging wind direction in the Southern Hemisphere, near-surface wind is affected by the pressure-gradient force and the geostrophic deflection force, and near a low pressure it is clockwise and slightly converges toward the low pressure; combined with the low-pressure center and the trend of the isobars in the figure, it can be judged that the prevailing wind in this sailing section is generally opposite to the course from Great Wall Station to Ushuaia, so it is against the wind. Looking at the water flow again, the Drake Passage is affected by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current, and the ocean current generally flows from west to east, while the ship going from Great Wall Station to Ushuaia has a westward sailing component, so the water flow is also opposite to the course, being against the current. Therefore, during the voyage it is against the wind and against the current.

method.method_draft: 先描述图像：在图上定位长城站、乌斯怀亚和两地之间的德雷克海峡，并观察该处等压线及附近低压中心。再推理：用南半球风向判读规则，由等压线和低压位置判断航段盛行风大致与船从长城站驶向乌斯怀亚的方向相反；再结合德雷克海峡南极绕极流自西向东，而船的航线具有向西到乌斯怀亚的分量，判断水流也与航向相反。因此得出逆风逆水。

推理：船只从长城站驶向乌斯怀亚，航向大致由南极半岛一侧指向南美南端，具有向北、向西的分量。根据南半球风向判读规则，近地面风受气压梯度力和地转偏向力影响，在低压附近呈顺时针方向并略向低压辐合；结合图中低压中心和等压线走向，可判断该航段盛行风总体与长城站到乌斯怀亚的航向相反，因此为逆风。再看水流，德雷克海峡受南极绕极流影响，洋流总体自西向东流动，而船由长城站去乌斯怀亚具有向西航行的分量，所以水流也与航向相反，为逆水。故航行过程中为逆风逆水。

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows the distribution of average sea-level pressure near Antarctica in January, marked with latitudes and longitudes such as 30°W, 60°W, 90°W and 30°S, 60°S. Great Wall Station is located near the Antarctic Peninsula, around about 60°S, and Ushuaia is located at the southern end of South America; between the two places is the Drake Passage. The isobars near the Great Wall Station–Ushuaia sailing section are relatively dense, and nearby there is a low-pressure center marked "Low", with pressure lines such as 984, 992, 1000, and 1004 visible around it.
Reasoning: The ship sails from Great Wall Station toward Ushuaia, and its course is roughly from the Antarctic Peninsula side toward the southern end of South America, with northward and westward components. According to the rule for judging wind direction in the Southern Hemisphere, near-surface wind is affected by the pressure-gradient force and the geostrophic deflection force, and near a low pressure it is clockwise and slightly converges toward the low pressure; combined with the low-pressure center and the trend of the isobars in the figure, it can be judged that the prevailing wind in this sailing section is generally opposite to the course from Great Wall Station to Ushuaia, so it is against the wind. Looking at the water flow again, the Drake Passage is affected by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current, and the ocean current generally flows from west to east, while the ship going from Great Wall Station to Ushuaia has a westward sailing component, so the water flow is also opposite to the course, being against the current. Therefore, during the voyage it is against the wind and against the current.
